title: Connectivity constraint categorizer and engagement lane for private/VPC/on-prem requests
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a lightweight, repeatable categorization and engagement workflow that triages incoming private/VPC/on-prem deployment requests based on connectivity constraints (egress, ingress, proxy, port restrictions, intermittent connectivity, and fully air-gapped). The goal is to reduce time-to-response, surface accurate implementation effort estimates to Sales/CS, and route customers to the appropriate support lane (self-serve probe, concierge, or engineered integration).

Scope: Non-bug customer requests for new Private/VPC/on-prem deployments and upgrade windows where networking constraints will affect rollout. Excludes incident/production outages (those follow incident runbooks). Covers: initial intake form fields, readiness scoring rubric, required artifacts, engagement lanes, templates, and metrics for success.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Intake form updated with connectivity signal fields and attachment points for artifacts (network diagram, ACLs, proxy configs).
- Scoring rubric implemented that maps incoming signal set to one of three lanes: Self-Serve (low friction), Concierge (medium friction, SE-assisted), Engineered Integration (high friction, requires eng time).
- SLA targets for initial triage: 24h for Self-Serve, 48h for Concierge, 72h for Engineered Integration initial plan.
- Probe library (reference) checklist published for customers and CS to run; automated readiness score returned in intake UI.
- Hand-off playbooks for Concierge and Engineered lanes with clear artifact and approval gates.

Proposed categorization dimensions (each weighted):
- Egress/ingress policy complexity (0-3): simple (0), few ports (1), multiple ports + NAT (2), cross-VPC/stacked firewalls (3).
- Persistent outbound availability (0-2): always available (0), intermittent or scheduled windows (1), only maintenance windows or no outbound (2).
- Proxy/inspection layer (0-2): none (0), standard corporate proxy (1), deep packet inspection / TLS inspection (2).
- Airgap/physical transfer required (0-3): no (0), optional offline transfer supported (1), strongly constrained (2), fully air-gapped with manual artifacts only (3).
- Administrative constraints (0-2): no special approvals (0), needs security/compliance sign-off (1), legal/third-party contracts required (2).

Score mapping to lane (example):
- 0-2: Self-Serve (provide step-by-step probe and automated checks)
- 3-6: Concierge (SE-led onboarding; scheduled remote network test)
- 7+: Engineered Integration (dedicated engineering ticket, on-site or bespoke proxy bridge)

Required intake artifacts by lane:
- Self-Serve: network diagram (simple), egress hostnames/IPs, maintenance windows
- Concierge: full firewall ACL exports, proxy auth flow, sample packet capture, contact windows
- Engineered Integration: architecture diagram, closed-loop runbook, escalation contacts, legal/compliance contact info

Automation & UX suggestions:
- Add discrete fields to intake: egress hosts, allowed ports, NAT use, proxy type, certificate pinning, offline transfer method.
- Implement small client-side network probe script customers can run; results attachable to intake to auto-fill scoring inputs.
- Intake UI should show preliminary lane and expected next steps and SLA.

Engagement lanes and handoffs:
- Self-Serve: CS email + automated checklist; if probe fails, escalate to Concierge.
- Concierge: schedule 1-hour SE network test, create a scoped plan, align on maintenance window; if blockers remain, escalate to Engineered Integration.
- Engineered Integration: open PM/ENG ticket (ENG-xxxx), assign engineering owner, estimate effort and schedule, create rollback plan and runbook.

Dependencies: security sign-off for any proxy-interaction playbook, infra tool to attach probe results to intake, and a small SE time budget. See dependencies field for keys.

Metrics of success (first 3 months):
- Reduce average time-to-triage from intake to assigned lane from ~4 business days to <48 hours.
- Increase % of requests resolved without eng time (Self-Serve or Concierge) from baseline by 25%.
- CS satisfaction score for onboarding process >= 4.2/5.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customers provide incomplete artifacts -> mitigation: enforce required attachments and provide a probe tool.
- Risk: Overly strict scoring misroutes customers -> mitigation: manual override by CS/PM and feedback loop for weight adjustments.
- Risk: Security-sensitive customers unwilling to run probes -> mitigation: SE-assisted remote tests and on-site/airgap procedures.

Next steps (first sprint):
1) Finalize field list for intake and probe output schema (owners: PM, DevX).
2) Draft scoring weights and thresholds and validate against 12 recent closed private-deploy requests.
3) Implement intake UI copy and automation hooks (CS webhook + Slack routing).
4) Prepare Concierge playbook and schedule 3 SE shadow sessions.

Longer term: Build readiness dashboard in Console showing queued private deploys with readiness score, and integrate with provisioning work so that high-readiness requests have faster runway into Dedicated/Private provisioning pipelines.
